title: Bataan Death March
summary: After the Bataan defenders were ordered to surrender on 9 April 1942, Japanese forces moved about 75,000 Filipino and American prisoners about 65 miles on foot from Mariveles to San Fernando, then by boxcar to Capas and on foot to Camp O'Donnell. Guards beat, shot and bayoneted prisoners. Sources give differing tolls: roughly 3,000 on the march (Army) to an estimated 17,000 during and after.

uncertainty.note: Surrender ordered 9 April 1942; the sources say the march took each group of about 100 around five days but give no start or end dates for the march itself.

as_recorded.value: rounded up by the Japanese in April 1942

where.modern_name: Mariveles, Bataan, Philippines (start of the march); route ran to San Fernando, Pampanga, then Capas, Tarlac
where.historical_name: Mariveles, Bataan Peninsula, Luzon, Philippine Commonwealth under Japanese military occupation

regions.name: San Fernando, Pampanga
regions.note: End of the walking portion; prisoners moved by boxcar

regions.name: Capas, Tarlac
regions.note: Rail stop; final seven miles on foot to Camp O'Donnell

importance.justification: Widely recognized as a major World War II war crime, killing thousands of Filipino and American prisoners.

audience_note: Describes the mass death, beatings, shootings and bayonetings of prisoners of war. Death tolls are estimates that differ by source.

sources.title: History of the Bataan Death March

beats.caption: On 9 April 1942 about 75,000 Filipino and American prisoners on Bataan were ordered to surrender to Japanese forces.
Prisoners walked about 65 miles to San Fernando, were packed into boxcars to Capas, then walked the final seven miles to the camp.
The Army account gives roughly 2,500 Filipino and 500 American deaths on the march, and many more at Camp O'Donnell.

reviewer_note: No source opened gives dated intermediate stops, so no path animation. Tolls: Army 2,500 Filipino + 500 American on the march, 26,000 Filipino + 1,500 American at Camp O'Donnell; History.com estimate 17,000 during and after, and VA figures of 650 American and 16,500 Filipino. Least sure: exact start day of the march.
